children.value: There are many occupations to pursue in geriatric care. Direct caregivers, primarily nurses, nurse assistants, therapists, and others, are in high demand. Other professionals are also necessary to ensure the best care is provided, including those in administration, social services, dietary and nutrition, care coordination, activities planning and various other support services. All of these roles have the potential to be deeply rewarding, because they all impact patient care in some way.
With an aging population, there are currently many opportunities in long-term care and assisted living, whether you’re looking for an entry-level position or a path to professional advancement.

inventory.text: Career Paths in Long-Term Care A Career in Long-Term Care Changing lives while you change your own There are many occupations to pursue in geriatric care. Direct caregivers, primarily nurses, nurse assistants, therapists, and others, are in high demand. Other professionals are also necessary to ensure the best care is provided, including those in administration, social services, dietary and nutrition, care coordination, activities planning and various other support services. All of these roles have the potential to be deeply rewarding, because they all impact patient care in some way. With an aging population, there are currently many opportunities in long-term care and assisted living, whether you’re looking for an entry-level position or a path to professional advancement. EXPLORE YOUR PATH Find the right career path for you Uncover your path to personal and professional fulfilment as you explore the diverse career opportunities in the dynamic field of long-term care. Discover a world of possibilities awaiting you in this rewarding industry. Certified Nurse Assistant The Certified Nurse Assistant (CNA) role is a vital part of senior living communities. CNAs provide hands-on compassionate care, ensuring the well-being of residents. CNAs are essential in healthcare and have opportunities for growth. Nursing Licensed Practical Nurses (LPNs) and Registered Nurses (RNs) provide professional medical care to residents with a personalized approach. Both requre professional degrees. Administration Administrators in senior living communities are responsible for overseeing the daily operations of the facility and ensuring all state and federal regulations are met. Social Services Social services personnel work with healthcare professionals to advocate for patients, support new residents in adjusting, and provide counseling. Therapy Therapists and related staff members work one-on-one with residents to improve mobility and strength. Care Coordination Care coordination staff work with new residents and their families. Their duties include admissions and customer service. Activities Activities directors and staff add a little fun to residential life. They plan and lead fun events to keep residents engaged. Support Services It takes many hands to ensure life runs smoothly in a senior care community. Laundry, maintenance, housekeeping and dietary staff members all play vital roles. Hey there! links.text: The Certified Nurse Assistant (CNA) role is a vital part of senior living communities. CNAs provide hands-on compassionate care, ensuring the well-being of residents. CNAs are essential in healthcare and have opportunities for growth.
Licensed Practical Nurses (LPNs) and Registered Nurses (RNs) provide professional medical care to residents with a personalized approach. Both requre professional degrees.
Administrators in senior living communities are responsible for overseeing the daily operations of the facility and ensuring all state and federal regulations are met.
Social services personnel work with healthcare professionals to advocate for patients, support new residents in adjusting, and provide counseling.
Therapists and related staff members work one-on-one with residents to improve mobility and strength.
Care coordination staff work with new residents and their families. Their duties include admissions and customer service.
Activities directors and staff add a little fun to residential life. They plan and lead fun events to keep residents engaged.
It takes many hands to ensure life runs smoothly in a senior care community. Laundry, maintenance, housekeeping and dietary staff members all play vital roles.
